stages.title: Self-assessment
stages.goal: Find out what you don't know yet, so you don't re-read what you already know.
intro: Answer each question on paper without looking anything up. The questions you can't answer are your personal study list: close them to L3 in the stage shown next to each one.
Redo this checklist every 3 months (one column per round) to see your progress.

items.text: I can explain the difference between a datum, an ellipsoid and a projection
I can explain why `buffer(500)` in EPSG:4326 is wrong
I can state the strengths and weaknesses of the vector and raster models
I know topology errors (gaps, overlaps, dangles) and how to fix them
I know the difference between spatial join predicates (intersects, within, contains, touches)
I can explain raster resolution, NoData and resampling methods
I know Tobler's law and what spatial autocorrelation is
I can interpret a Moran's I result
I can explain MAUP (results change when zone boundaries change) with an example
I can compute the difference between Euclidean and network (road) distance
I know why a random train/test split inflates accuracy on spatial data
I know what bands and indices (NDVI) mean in satellite imagery
I know the difference between segmentation and detection
I can name 2 ways to measure "accessibility"
I know what population density and land-use mix affect

stages.title: GeoAI on vector and tabular data
stages.goal: "How good is this location for X" problems (GeoScore type): your ML knowledge takes its spatial form here.
callouts: The most important rule: on spatial data a random train/test split inflates accuracy, because nearby points land in both sets. Meyer and Pebesma (2022, Nature Communications) showed the problem in how global ML maps are evaluated. Spatial CV is itself debated, and some researchers argue it isn't always the right answer: try both and measure the difference yourself.

items.practice: Read one GeoPandas or rasterio error and name the library behind it

callouts: Know the OSGeo ecosystem: OSGeo is the umbrella organization for QGIS, GDAL/OGR, GEOS, PostGIS, GeoServer and pgRouting. Almost every library you use (GeoPandas, shapely, rasterio) relies on GDAL, GEOS and PROJ under the hood, so knowing them at L2 makes errors much easier to understand. Its education initiative is Geo for All; its annual conference is FOSS4G (talks are free on YouTube).

stages.title: LLMs and GIS
stages.goal: The newest and fastest-growing direction: LLMs that turn a task in plain language into spatial analysis.
intro: Li and Ning (2023) proposed "Autonomous GIS": an LLM turns a natural-language task into spatial analysis code and runs it. Since then came the data-retrieval agent LLM-Find, GIS Copilot inside QGIS, and several benchmarks. Even the best models struggle with complex multi-step spatial reasoning, so the field still has plenty of open problems.

groups.label: A classic, slowly: Jane Jacobs, The Death and Life of Great American Cities
groups.note: 1–2 chapters a month. After each chapter ask yourself: "Which indicator could measure this idea?" That question is where urban analytics and GeoAI meet.

items.text: Part One: The peculiar nature of cities
Part Two: The conditions for city diversity
Part Three: Forces of decline and regeneration
Part Four: Different tactics

callouts: Local context: don't copy Western methodologies blindly. Tashkent's mahalla system, informal commerce, summer heat and Soviet-era microdistricts are distinctive. For every imported indicator, check: "Does this work the same way in Tashkent?"

stages.title: Capstone projects and portfolio
stages.goal: Each stage closes with one visible result. Everything goes on GitHub, with a README and a map.

items.title: School accessibility: buffer vs network distance
Apartment price / cafe success model with spatial CV
Mahalla green cover and LST maps
End-to-end platform: data → model → API → web map, or a research paper

callouts: Paper route for the final capstone: project 1 or 3 can become a research paper. Suitable venues: Computers, Environment and Urban Systems; Environment and Planning B: Urban Analytics and City Science; the FOSS4G Academic Track. GeoAI research on Central Asian cities is very scarce: that's your advantage.
